title: Safeguarding Public Monies Given to Town Councils
what_it_is: Safeguarding Public Monies Given to Town Councils

sections.label: KPMG report on AHTC control failures
sections.summary: KPMG's July 2016 report found 185 control failures in AHTC, 115 from earlier audits and 70 newly uncovered, described as pervasive across five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: In its July 2016 report, KPMG reported a total of 185 control failures in AHTC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This comprises 115 identified by AHTC's statutory auditors and the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) in previous audits, and an additional 70 control failures uncovered by KPMG.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: KPMG concluded that AHTC's control failures were "pervasive, cutting across the key areas of governance, financial control, financial reporting, procurement and records management over the course of five years".

sections.label: Town Councils Act review areas
sections.summary: The ongoing Town Councils Act review aims to finish within the year and focuses on three areas: subordination to public authorities, governance and financial accountability, and MND oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Town Councils Act review is ongoing and we aim to complete the review by the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As the then Minister for National Development Mr Khaw Boon Wan had articulated, I believe at the opening of the Parliamentary debate of the Auditor-General's report, he said that the Town Council Act review ought to focus on three areas, principally: first, it would make clear that Town Councils are subordinate to and must comply with public authorities charged with public duties; second, to strengthen the Town Councils' corporate governance and financial accountability framework; and third, to strengthen MND's regulatory oversight and the powers to obtain information and conduct investigations, as well as to look at the overall penalty framework.

sections.label: Handover process and boundary changes
sections.summary: The review will further examine the handover process, as boundary changes across political lines may cause delays in accounts and documents that affect the receiving Town Council's audits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In particular, we will further look at the handover process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We understand that when boundaries change, especially across political lines, delays in submission of accounts and documents may impact the financial audits of the receiving Town Council.

sections.label: AGC letter to town councils
sections.summary: After the Court of Appeal judgment, the Attorney-General's Chambers wrote to AHTC and PRPTC on behalf of HDB on 4 December 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Following the Court of Appeal judgment, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC), on behalf of HDB, had written to AHTC and PRPTC on 4 December 2015.

sections.label: Court of Appeal on accountant nominations
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal heard on 22 January 2016 that each AHTC-nominated firm had a member who failed ACRA's PMP inspection, and directed AHTC to appoint a Big Four firm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Page: 10 The Court of Appeal eventually heard evidence on 22 January 2016 that both of AHTC's nominated firms of accountants each had a member who had failed ACRA's PMP inspection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Agreeing that AHTC's nomination approach suggested a lack of rigour and basic due diligence, the Court of Appeal then directed AHTC to appoint one of the Big Four firms as the matter was of public interest and involved public funds.

sections.label: Court of Appeal ruling on PRPTC
sections.summary: On 8 July 2016 the Court of Appeal ruled PRPTC had an interest in KPMG's work and directed the two accountants to communicate directly and provide access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On 8 July 2016, the Court of Appeal ruled that PRPTC, on behalf of Punggol East, had an interest in the outcome of the work carried out by KPMG and because the issue of joint appointment, as the Member had alluded to, was already moot by then, the Court of Appeal directed that the two accountants communicate directly with each other to provide each other access as may reasonably be required to safeguard each other's interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first clarification to make is that the Senior Minister of State mentioned in his answer earlier that AHTC had been reluctant to appoint a Big Four firm but, based on his answer, I think he will confirm that the requirement to appoint a Big Four firm was only clarified in January this year when the Court of Appeal subsequently explained further its view on the matter, on which accounting firm it felt was suitable.

sections.label: Town Councils submit management letters
sections.summary: The Ministry annually requires Town Councils to submit financial statements and auditors' management letters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A further supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State: I understand that the Ministry annually requires Town Councils to submit not just their financial statements but also their Page: 11 management letters issued by the auditors to each Town Council.

sections.label: KPMG report and circular
sections.summary: After KPMG's April 2016 report, the Senior Minister of State sent a circular to Town Council Chairmen with slides.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Last of all, Madam, it was interesting to me that when KPMG issued their first report in April 2016, and shortly after that in May, the Senior Minister of State himself actually sent a circular to all Town Council Chairmen attaching some slides and saying that Town Councils might want to use these slides to brief their Town Councillors on their roles and responsibilities, especially the key committees involved in finance and governance.

sections.label: AGO findings on AHPETC
sections.summary: AGO made findings of concern on AHPETC, with no assurance that accounts are accurate or funds properly managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: AGO also made many findings of concern on AHPETC, and, in fact, I have articulated a summary of AGO's findings, which is that there is no assurance that AHTC's accounts are accurate or reliable, or that public funds are properly spent, accounted for and managed.

sections.label: High Court grave questions
sections.summary: The High Court stated there are grave and serious questions about the accounts and related-party payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The High Court, for instance, in its judgment, stated, and I quote: "there are grave and serious questions" about the state of accounts and whether payments to related parties were valid or proper".

sections.label: KPMG July report concerns
sections.summary: KPMG, appointed by AHTC under the Court of Appeal's order, raised serious concerns in its July report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2016, we have KPMG which is appointed by AHTC, in compliance with limb one of the Court of Appeal's orders, and in that respect, the latest report in July raised serious concerns and this was what we articulated in the Parliamentary Question reply earlier.

sections.label: Recovering monies and accountants
sections.summary: The speaker asks when AHTC was told HDB agreed with PRPTC to appoint accountants, noting liberty to apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Indeed, if they find that there are payments which ought to be recovered and there were lost monies, then it is our duty to go and recover them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State when was this information that HDB had agreed with PRPTC to appoint accountants made known to AHTC?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And if the joint appointment of accountants was indeed so important to HDB, the Court of Appeal's judgment of 27 November 2015 allows HDB, MND and AHTC liberty to apply to the Court.

sections.label: Workers' Party overpayment claims
sections.summary: A Member asks why the Workers' Party now says improper payments may warrant clawback from FMSS, after saying in 2015 there were no overpayments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Some of us recall, and we may be wrong, that during the General Elections in 2015, various Members from the Workers' Party or the AHPETC had said that there were no overpayments at all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, why now the Member's position that there could possibly be "improper" payments, not just improper but that will warrant it being clawed back from FMSS?
